newsitem.title: GERMANY: Germany's Waigel says there will be no soft euro.
newsitem.headline: Germany's Waigel says there will be no soft euro.

text.p: German Finance Minister Theo Waigel said on Friday that the treaty signed at the European Union's Amsterdam summit ensured economic and monetary union would launch a stable currency.
"There will be no soft euro," Waigel told parliament. "We will not allow a softening of the Maastricht criteria."

Waigel said there was no automatic plan for which countries would be able to participate in EMU from the start, and that the decision would not be made until the spring of 1998, based on actual data for this year, not forecasts or estimates.
He said recent statements by French premier Lionel Jospin and Finance Minister Dominique Strauss-Kahn showed they were committed to meeting the EMU budget targets.
But he did not mention Strauss-Kahn's statement that France's 1997 deficit would be over 3.0 percent of gross domestic product.
